DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, CFO $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252-day beta of about 0.1, a defensive single-stock position. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries SIC mislabel (bucket Consumer Discretionary), so the case rests on absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. It fails leverage_not_up. It is the largest single position. The only lot opened 2026-10-20 and is short-term until 2027-10-21, so there is no tax reason to hold. Sentiment items, not 8-K events: EVP and Chief Restaurant Officer stock sale (11-23) and BNP Paribas Underperform initiation with a $295 PT (11-24). Next earnings 2027-02-22 (file estimate).
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes at or below $335 (about 5.8% above the $316.58 fill), or a fundamentals screen drops it from the menu or shows CFO below net income, or a confirmed guidance cut.

I accepted the Skeptic's concentration objection: DPZ is the largest single name at 11.9%, with a BNP Underperform ($295 PT) and an EVP sale. The stop moves up to $335, about 6% under the $356.52 mark, which is outside daily noise for a 0.11-beta name.

TLT.thesis: A defensive Treasury sleeve while the regime filter allows only BND, GLD, IEF and TLT. The Market Analyst (risk-off) calls Treasuries the one sleeve hedging. TLT is used because IEF and BND are wash-sale blocked, not because he prefers it; he calls intermediate duration the steadier hedge. TLT tracks 20+ year Treasuries and is judged not substantially identical to the blocked IEF. It carries long-duration rate risk that the beta-based stress test does not show. Plan for the 12-09 FOMC (hikes priced): hold through it unless a stored clause trips; no further adds. It is the only bond holding and has its own stop (L9). ETF, no earnings events.
